evidence_scope: Documented API surface plus inspected adapter behavior; not server source inspection or live response verification.

R2.reason: Inspected documentation defines a Web Search request, but does not explicitly attest the absence of all server-side decomposition, expansion or hidden follow-up queries required by the strict WO text. Client single-call tests do not establish this server-side property.

R7.reason: Optional enhanced product surfaces can be excluded in the request. The inspected documents do not establish the stronger absence-of-undeclared-stack guarantee; a mock does not close that evidence gap.

hash_scope: Fingerprints cover these compact paraphrased records, not the complete provider webpages.
limitations: Live index, ranking and pages can drift even with an API contract version pinned.
Optional server-side additions can appear; non-web/enhanced material is excluded or rejected by this adapter.
A mock response cannot establish deployed behavior, availability, latency, pricing or account entitlement.
US locale is a candidate profile, not approval of the parent T6 task geography.
Public documentation is not proof about undisclosed provider internals.

records.observation_qualification: Observation-date anchor; not asserted as the server modification time.
propositions: Web Search is a GET endpoint with an explicit q input and configurable count.
spellcheck can be disabled; enabled correction can use an altered query.
result_filter can select web results while query metadata is still returned.
Goggles reranking, summaries and extra snippets are optional surfaces, not necessary to request ordinary web results.
A caller can select an Api-Version date; omission uses the latest version.
The documented request includes locale, language, safety and optional enhancement controls.

records.observation_qualification: Observation-date anchor; not asserted as the server modification time.
propositions: The official versioning example explicitly sends Api-Version with value 2023-01-01.
The guide describes a header-selected API contract; an omitted header selects latest.
Optional additions may be backward compatible; removals and type changes require a breaking-version change.
